source.title: Director of Quality
source.description:
Description:

**Built** **on** **Experience.** **Built** **for** **Skill.** **Built** **for You.**

Keel was formed by bringing together three industry leaders combining generations of hands-on expertise in steel fabrication, shipbuilding, aerospace, and defense manufacturing.

That means when you join Keel, you’re joining a team backed by decades of proven craftsmanship and real-world results.

We build ships, defense systems, aerospace components, and heavy steel structures that serve critical missions — and we do it with pride.

**Your Mission:**

The Director of Quality provides strategic leadership, technical oversight, and compliance governance for multiple heavy fabrication plants producing structural weldments, assemblies, and machined components for the Nuclear Navy. This role ensures full alignment with ISO 9001, NAVSEA, and customer specific requirements.

**Explore the Depth of the Role:**

* Provide strategic leadership for quality operations across three South Carolina fabrication facilities supporting U.S. Navy shipbuilding and defense manufacturing programs.
* Ensure all products meet contractual, technical, regulatory, NAVSEA, and quality requirements while driving continuous improvement in customer satisfaction and product performance.
* Lead the development, implementation, and continual improvement of the Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure compliance with customer, industry, and regulatory requirements.
* Serve as the primary quality interface for customers, government representatives, auditors, and regulatory agencies, leading quality reviews, audits, corrective actions, and performance discussions.
* Direct all quality assurance, quality control, inspection, test, dimensional verification, NDT, welding quality, and supplier quality activities across the region.
* Establish and monitor quality performance metrics including First-Time Quality (FTQ), Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), defect escapes, rework, audit findings, and inspection cycle time.
* Lead root cause analysis, corrective action, and continuous improvement initiatives to eliminate recurring nonconformances and improve manufacturing performance.
* Drive operational excellence through improved inspection efficiency, resource utilization, process standardization, and deployment of risk-based quality methodologies.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Program Management teams to proactively prevent defects and improve overall manufacturing effectiveness.
* Build and sustain a culture where quality, compliance, workmanship excellence, and customer focus are integrated into daily operations at all levels of the organization.
* Recruit, develop, coach, and lead Quality Managers, Engineers, Supervisors, Auditors, and Inspectors while building organizational capability and succession plans.
* Other related duties as assigned.

Requirements:

**Mission Readiness:**

* Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, or related technical discipline; Master's Degree preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive quality leadership experience in shipbuilding, defense, defense manufacturing, heavy fabrication, aerospace, or similar industries.
* Demonstrated experience leading multi-site quality organizations.
* Root cause analysis and corrective action applied to nonconformances and recurring defects
* Quality auditing, including internal, supplier, and customer audit planning, execution, and follow-up
* Data analysis and reporting using quality metrics, dashboards, and tools such as Excel, Power BI, and ERP/QMS software
* Contract and technical document review, including drawings, specifications, work instructions, and inspection plans
* Executive-level presentation and negotiation skills for customer meetings, corrective action reviews, and dispute resolution
* Quality Management Systems: AS9100, ISO 9001, Navy QA requirements, nonconformance management, and CAPA
* Welding and NDT Oversight: Weld procedures, inspection methods, and material traceability in accordance with NAVSEA requirements
* Supplier Quality: Qualifying, auditing, and developing suppliers; preventing counterfeit or nonconforming material
* Regulatory and Contract Compliance: Government source inspection, DCMA surveillance, and audit readiness
* Continuous Improvement and Leadership: Lean, Six Sigma, root cause analysis, and developing quality talent
* Track and report cost of quality (prevention, appraisal, internal and external failure) and drive reductions in rework and scrap
* Support program pricing, proposals, and forecasts with accurate quality labor and resource estimates
* Evaluate the cost, schedule, and risk impact of quality decisions, such as rework, repair, and corrective action investments

*Travel Requirements:*

Between facilities as needed

*Physical Requirements:*

* May be required to stand, walk, sit, reach/pull/push with hands and arms, climb or balance, stoop or kneel regularly.
* May lift or carry 50lbs. Weights exceeding 50lbs will require mechanical means to maneuver.

**Become** **a** **part** **of** **our** **Builders** **and** **you** **too** **can...**

* Uphold Safety and Quality Standards
* Embody Team Spirit
* Relentless Customer Focus
* Convey Integrity, Trust, and Professionalism
* Execute with Excellence and Velocity

**What** **Keel** **will** **build** **for** **you:**

* Comprehensive Benefit Package
* Competitive Pay
* 401(k) Match
* HSA/FSA
* Paid Holidays
* Paid Time Off
* Internal Referral Bonus Opportunities
* Shift Differentials
* Overtime Potential
* Paid on the Job Training
* Certification Sponsorship Opportunities
* Committed to Individual Career Growth
* We Do Fun Things, Plus More!

**Need** **Assistance?**

If you require a reasonable accommodation at any stage of the employment process, please email talent@keelusa.com with details about your request and your contact information. Accommodation requests are reviewed individually on a case-by-case basis. Please note that this email address is monitored only for inquiries related to reasonable accommodation requests.

*Equal* *Opportunity* *Employer* */* *Individuals* *with* *Disabilities* */* *Protected Veterans*

**What** **we** **build,** **builds us.**

source.title: Director of Production - Headset and Battery
source.description:
Unusual Machines is a U.S.-based drone and drone parts company focused on the small and First-Person View (FPV) segments of the drone market. Our brands - Rotor Riot, Fat Shark, Rotor Lab and - coming soon - Upgrade Energy - are some of the most respected names in FPV and have helped shape the industry through e-commerce, product development, and a deep connection with the pilot community.
 
 
We’re expanding into enterprise and defense - bringing our obsessive attention to performance, design, and U.S.-based manufacturing into high-stakes environments like search and rescue and military innovation. With several of our products already approved by the Defense Innovation Unit, we’re solving procurement issues for customers who demand speed, agility, and compliance.
 
 
If you love working at the intersection of community, content, and cutting-edge technology, you’ll feel right at home here.
 
 
Director of Production
 
 
**Location:**
Orlando, Florida
 
 
Who You Are
 
 
You are an experienced manufacturing leader who knows how to turn complex hardware into a repeatable, scalable production operation.
 
 
You’re equally comfortable setting the strategy and getting on the production floor to solve problems. You thrive in fast-moving environments, build strong teams, and bring structure, accountability, and continuous improvement to everything you do.
 
 
You have experience leading production of complex hardware—ideally electronics, electromechanical products, batteries, drones, robotics, aerospace, or similar—and understand what it takes to scale from early production to meaningful volume.
 
 
What You’ll Do
 
 

* Own production operations for our FPV headsets, cameras, and renewable/rechargeable battery assemblies in Orlando.
* Build and lead a high-performing production team, including supervisors, leads, specialists, and assembly personnel.
* Establish the processes, systems, staffing, and production standards needed to scale.
* Own production planning, capacity, throughput, quality, yield, labor efficiency, and on-time delivery.
* Develop standardized work, assembly processes, testing procedures, and production KPIs.
* Identify bottlenecks and drive continuous improvement across the production floor.
* Partner closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Development to ensure products are designed and built for manufacturing.
* Lead the introduction of new products and processes into production.
* Evaluate tooling, equipment, automation, and capital investments that improve capacity, quality, and cost.
* Build a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

What You’ll Bring
 
 

* 8+ years of progressive manufacturing or production leadership experience.
* Experience scaling production operations and building manufacturing teams and processes.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, and production KPIs.
* Experience with complex hardware, electronics, batteries, aerospace, drones, robotics, or similar products preferred.
* Experience with NPI, DFM/DFA, production testing, and manufacturing process development.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and organizational skills.
* Experience working with ERP/MRP and production planning systems.
* A hands-on leadership style with the ability to move between strategic planning and solving issues on the production floor.
* A bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, business, or a related field is preferred.

What Does Success Look Like?
 
 
**In Your First 6 Months, You Will**

* Build a strong, accountable battery production organization.
* Establish scalable processes and standardized work across all product lines.
* Create clear production metrics and operating rhythms.
* Improve throughput, yield, quality, and on-time delivery.
* Establish reliable capacity and labor planning.
* Identify and remove the biggest constraints to growth.
* Create a roadmap for automation, tooling, and production investment.
* Partner with Engineering to make our products easier, faster, and more cost-effective to manufacture.
* Establish a production operation that is safe, predictable, scalable, and ready for the next stage of growth.

**Compensation -**
130,000.00 - 160,000.00
 
 
**Benefits**

* Equity
* Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits
* 401(k)
* Generous PTO
* Paid Holidays
* Daily Catered Lunches

*We are an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.*
*Unusual Machines participates in E-Verify. E-Verify is an Internet-based system that compares information from an employee's Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification, to data from U.S. Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration records to confirm employment eligibility.*
*Candidates must be a US Citizen or permanent resident to be eligible for employment*

source.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing
source.description:
**Hyve Company Overview**
Hyve Solutions transforms complex engineering challenges into production reality for technology innovators building AI, cloud, and connected infrastructure. As a US-based manufacturing partner, the company rapidly delivers fast, agile execution through dep technical partnerships and co-innovation, and supply chain clarity. Hyve’s integrated ODM, CM, and SI capabilities eliminate vendor complexity while accelerating time-to-market with single-partner accountability from design through scale. The company co-innovates with deep engineering expertise, treating customer success as its own while building tomorrow's digital infrastructure.
 
 
****Position Summary****
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing provides strategic and operational leadership for manufacturing execution, workforce planning, quality, cost, delivery, and continuous improvement. This role translates demand and customer requirements into executable production plans, leads manufacturing teams, and partners across Supply Chain, Quality, Engineering, Program Management, and Human Resources to deliver safe, efficient, scalable, and high-quality operations.
 
 
****Hyve Company Overview****
Hyve Solutions transforms complex engineering challenges into production reality for technology innovators building AI, cloud, and connected infrastructure. As a US-based manufacturing partner, the company rapidly delivers fast, agile execution through deep technical partnerships and co-innovation, and supply chain clarity. Hyve's integrated ODM, CM, and SI capabilities eliminate vendor complexity while accelerating time-to-market with single-partner accountability from design through scale. The company co-innovates with deep engineering expertise, treating customer success as its own while building tomorrow's digital infrastructure.
 
 
**Compensation:**
The anticipated base salary range for this position is
**$135,000K-$169,000K annually**
. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, qualifications, and business needs
 
 
****Key Responsibilities****

* Develop and execute the manufacturing strategy for assigned operations in alignment with the company’s mission, values, and business goals. Continuously improve manufacturing processes for efficiency and scalability.
* Create production plans, schedules, and budgets to meet product demand while maintaining quality, cost, and on-time delivery requirements.
* Develop and implement manufacturing headcount requirements and hiring plans based on forecasts, demand plans, yields, cycle times, capacity, and shift needs.
* Implement and maintain quality-control measures throughout the manufacturing process. Establish quality standards, monitor performance, and address issues in partnership with Quality and Engineering.
* Collaborate with Supply Chain to manage component procurement, inventory levels, material availability, and vendor support for production needs.
* Control manufacturing costs by identifying cost-saving opportunities, supporting supplier negotiations, and managing approved budgets.
* Maintain knowledge of applicable industry regulations, safety standards, environmental requirements, and company policies. Ensure assigned operations meet established requirements.
* Drive continuous-improvement initiatives to improve manufacturing efficiency, product quality, cost, and sustainability. Apply Lean manufacturing principles and appropriate technologies where applicable.
* Identify and mitigate manufacturing risks to support a resilient and adaptable operation.
* Lead and develop manufacturing managers, supervisors, leads, and production teams. Set clear expectations and accountability across assigned shifts and areas.
* Use manufacturing data and performance metrics to make decisions and communicate results, risks, and support needs to leadership.

****Required Qualifications****

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including manufacturing leadership experience.
* Experience in manufacturing leadership roles, preferably in consumer electronics, printed circuit board, server, storage, networking, rack-integration, or related manufacturing environments.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, production planning, quality management, cost control, capacity planning, labor planning, and environmental or sustainability practices.
* Demonstrated experience leading and developing managers, supervisors, leads, or multi-shift production teams.
* Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
* Strong problem-solving skills and a data-driven approach to decision-making.
* Familiarity with industry-standard manufacturing, ERP/MRP, reporting, data-analysis, and supply-chain tools or systems.

****Preferred Qualifications****

* Master’s degree or MBA.
* Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, structured problem-solving, new-product-introduction, or manufacturing-automation experience.
* Experience supporting customer audits, regulatory requirements, environmental initiatives, or multi-site manufacturing operations.
* Commitment to continuous improvement, responsible manufacturing, and the company’s mission and values.

**Work Environment and Physical Expectations**
This role operates in both office and manufacturing-floor environments. Business needs may require extended hours, support across shifts, occasional evenings or weekends, and travel for business, customer, or training purposes. The employee must be able to safely access and work within assigned manufacturing areas. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
 
 
What’s in it for you
 
 
Benefit Insurance
 
 

* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* Mental Health Care
* 401K with match
* Paid Holidays, Vacation & Sick Days
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Perks at Work
* LEAP Program
* MyFlexPay

*We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.*

source.title: Senior Manager of Manufacturing Product & Test Engineering
source.description:
**Job Description**
The Senior Manager of Manufacturing Product & Test Engineering is a leadership role responsible for ensuring that products are designed, validated, and manufactured with robust, scalable, and cost-effective test solutions. This leader will lead product engineering, test engineering, and new product introduction (NPI) through mass production activities within manufacturing, ensuring seamless transition from design to high-volume production. The role partners closely with design, quality, and external partners to deliver high-quality, reliable products while optimizing test coverage, yield, and cost.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Key Responsibilities**

* Strategic Leadership & Execution

+ Lead NPI readiness and manufacturing ramp strategies to ensure successful product launches.

* Product Engineering

+ Oversee product engineering activities supporting manufacturing, including BOM management, configuration control, and engineering change implementation (ECO/ECN).
+ Ensure design for manufacturability (DFM), design for testability (DFT), and design for reliability (DFR) principles are embedded in product development.
+ Drive root cause analysis and resolution of product-related issues in production and the field.

* Test Engineering & Validation

+ Lead the development and deployment of manufacturing test strategies, including functional, parametric, environmental, and reliability testing.
+ Optimize test coverage, cycle time, and cost while maintaining product quality and compliance.
+ Oversee test equipment design, validation, calibration, and lifecycle management.
+ Implement advanced test technologies, automation, and data analytics to improve efficiency and insight.

* New Product Introduction (NPI)

+ Partner with design to ensure smooth product transfers from development to manufacturing.
+ Establish robust validation processes and pilot builds.
+ Drive readiness reviews, risk assessments, and launch performance tracking.

* Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

+ Champion Lean, Six Sigma, and data-driven methodologies to improve yield, throughput, and reliability.
+ Identify and eliminate production inefficiencies and test bottlenecks.
+ Establish KPIs and dashboards for product performance, test efficiency, and manufacturing readiness.

* Cross-Functional Collaboration

+ Collaborate with Quality, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Operations to ensure alignment on product requirements and execution.
+ Support supplier selection and qualification for test equipment and capabilities.
+ Act as a key liaison between engineering and manufacturing teams globally.

* Team Leadership & Development

+ Build, lead, and mentor high-performing product and test engineering teams across multiple locations.
+ Develop organizational capability in advanced test engineering, data analytics, and product support.
+ Drive a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous learning.

**Qualifications**

* Education & Experience

+ Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Electrical, Computer, or related field); Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
+ 8-10+ years of experience in product engineering or test engineering, with at least 5+ years in a management role.
+ Proven track record supporting complex product portfolios.

* Technical Expertise

+ Deep knowledge of product lifecycle management (PLM), configuration control, and engineering change processes.
+ Strong expertise in manufacturing test methodologies, test system design, and validation processes.
+ Experience with DFM, DFT, DFR, and reliability engineering principles.
+ Familiarity with automation, data acquisition systems, and Industry 4.0 technologies.
+ Background in test automation, software-driven testing, and data analytics platforms.

* Leadership & Business Acumen

+ Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and execution capabilities.
+ Financial acumen, including capital planning and cost optimization.
+ Track record of successful product launches and manufacturing scale-ups.

* Skills & Competencies

+ Excellent analytical and troubleshooting skills.
+ Ability to manage complex programs and competing priorities.
+ High level of integrity, accountability, and adaptability.

source.description:
**Position Purpose**

The Senior Manager leads the global Advanced Manufacturing Technology (AMT) organization and converts long-range technical direction into an executable three-to-five-year portfolio of technology, automation, equipment, and factory-transformation initiatives.

The role owns people leadership, portfolio execution, global capital-process stewardship, strategic vendor and technical-equipment vendor portfolio management, deployment, adoption, and business results.

**Principal Accountabilities**

**Strategy and Portfolio Leadership**

Translate enterprise strategy and technical direction into an executable AMT roadmap.

Prioritize initiatives using business value, readiness, risk, capacity, and strategic alignment.

Drive results across functions, regions, and multiple levels.

**Global Capital Process Custodianship**

Serve as custodian of the global capital process, including standard work, governance, review cadence, documentation quality, portfolio transparency, and continuous improvement.

Develop and quality-review investment plans, business cases, and Capital Expenditure Requests (CERs).

Provide the Vice President portfolio analysis and recommendations supporting global capital strategy and prioritization.

Manage assigned capital and operating budgets and ensure financial adherence.

**Global Vendor and Technical Equipment Portfolio**

Lead strategic relationships with key global manufacturing-technology and equipment vendors.

Create and maintain the technical equipment vendor portfolio, including preferred capabilities, technology coverage, performance, quality, delivery, risk, capacity, lifecycle support, and regional applicability.

Lead supplier development, technical reviews, commercial alignment, long-term service strategies, and executive escalation.

Use global portfolio leverage to improve standardization, innovation access, total cost, delivery, and support.

**Technology Deployment and Results**

Lead programs from concept approval through industrialization, qualification, deployment, adoption, and benefits realization.

Establish accountability for scope, schedule, budget, risk, and measurable outcomes.

Remove organizational barriers and ensure consistent execution across regions.

**Organization and Talent**

Lead, coach, and develop.

Build morale, productivity, innovation, learning, succession, and accountability.

**AMT Expansion Playbook**

Create and maintain the AMT expansion playbook covering organizational, people, technical, process, specification, vendor, equipment, installation, qualification, training, and readiness requirements.

Own the AMT workstream for expansion programs and ensure equipment and technology readiness at each stage gate.

**Nature and Scope**

The Senior Manager leads the global AMT organization with broad accountability for organizational capability, global capital-process stewardship, key vendor relationships, the technical-equipment vendor portfolio, technology investment execution, deployment, and measurable business outcomes across regions.

**Knowledge & Skills**

**Education & Experience**

Bachelor degree in Engineering required; advanced degree preferred.

12+ years in manufacturing technology, automation, industrialization, or related fields.

5+ years leading technical teams and complex cross-functional programs.

**Technical & Functional Expertise**

Manufacturing technologies, automation, controls, robotics, digital manufacturing, industrialization, equipment-vendor management, capital governance, and portfolio management.

Strong working knowledge of Lean and high-variation, low-volume manufacturing.

**Leadership & Business Competencies**

Compelling vision, stakeholder mobilization, financial acumen, talent development, change leadership, and three-to-five-year strategic planning.

**Working Conditions**

Office and manufacturing environments.

Standing and walking up to 50 percent; occasional lifting up to 30 pounds.

Domestic and international travel up to 30 percent.

 

BAC Hiring Compensation Range $133,300 - $228,600 
 
BAC offers a comprehensive benefits package to include medical, dental, vision, paid time off, 401k, employee stock ownership plan, and more. Please see additional details on the BAC website at www.Baltimoreaircoil.com. 
 
BAC Employees are eligible to participate in an annual bonus incentive program.

Equal Opportunity Employer

source.description:
**Lead Operations. Build Teams. Drive Growth.**

Are you a hands-on operations leader who thrives on building high-performing teams, improving processes, and delivering results? UFP Factory Built is looking for a Plant Manager to lead one of our manufacturing facilities and play a key role in the success of our growing business.

 

As a Plant Manager, you'll have the opportunity to run the operation like it's your own, leading production, safety, quality, inventory, maintenance, and team development while making a direct impact on profitability and customer satisfaction. This is an ideal role for a leader who enjoys solving problems, developing people, and creating a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

**About UFP Factory Built**

UFP Factory Built, a division of UFP Industries, supplies structural components and engineered solutions for manufactured housing, modular construction, RV, and cargo trailer manufacturers throughout North America. We are part of a stable, growth-oriented organization with a strong reputation for investing in our people and promoting from within.

 

### **What You'll Do**

* Lead all day-to-day plant operations, ensuring safety, quality, productivity, and profitability goals are achieved.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of supervisors and production employees.
* Drive operational excellence through process improvements, waste reduction, and efficiency initiatives.
* Manage production scheduling, inventory levels, shipping activities, and resource planning.
* Monitor key performance metrics and take action to improve throughput, quality, and financial results.
* Partner with leadership on capital investments, facility improvements, and business growth initiatives.
* Foster a culture centered around safety, employee engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with company policies, OSHA standards, and all applicable regulations.
Oversee maintenance programs to maximize equipment reliability and minimize downtime. 

 

### **What We're Looking For**

* Experience leading manufacturing, production, operations, or industrial teams.
* Proven ability to motivate employees, develop talent, and drive results.
* Strong business acumen with experience managing budgets, costs, and operational metrics.
* Ability to identify opportunities, solve problems, and implement effective solutions.
* Experience with inventory management, production scheduling, and process improvement.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, and Outlook.
Forklift certification or willingness to obtain certification. 

 

### **Why Join UFP?**

* Opportunity to lead and influence all aspects of a manufacturing operation.
* High visibility and direct impact on business performance.
* Stable and growing company with a strong national footprint.
* Collaborative culture that values leadership, innovation, and accountability.
* Career advancement opportunities within UFP Industries.
Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits package. 

 

### **What Success Looks Like**

In this role, you'll build a safe, efficient, and engaged operation, develop future leaders, improve plant performance, and help position the facility for continued growth. You'll have the autonomy to make decisions, the support of an experienced leadership team, and the opportunity to leave a lasting impact on the business.

 

**If you're a driven operations leader looking to take ownership of a facility, develop teams, and grow your career with an industry leader, we'd love to hear from you.**

**Benefits** **currently offered to our employees:**

* Medical Insurance
* Health Savings Account with Company Contribution
* Dental Insurance
* Vision Insurance
* Basic and Voluntary Life Insurance
* Disability Insurance
* 401(k) plan with Company Match
* Paid Vacation and Holidays
* Stock Purchase Program with Employee Discount
* Education Reimbursement
* Wellness Programs and Challenges
Other Supplemental Benefits 

*The Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer.*

Department: EPC Business Unit
 
 
Location: Houston, TX
 
 
Supervisor: COO

Work Status: Hybrid
 
 
SVP, ENVIRONMENT, SAFETY, HEALTH & QUALITY (ESHQ)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (Qcells USA), headquartered in Houston, TX, specializes in providing utility-scale modules, solar photovoltaic (PV), and battery energy storage systems (BESS) project development, along with Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) services for solar and BESS projects nationwide. Qcells USA delivers comprehensive turnkey solutions encompassing the entire utility-scale project lifecycle. By choosing Qcells USA for turnkey solutions, customers can reduce uncertainty and risk, leading to enhanced investment returns and contributing to a more sustainable future.
 
 
Qcells USA’s complete turnkey solutions seamlessly integrate the expertise of our Development, Module, and EPC teams, while ensuring close coordination with other vital internal groups such as Project Finance, Systems Integration, and Legal. This collaborative approach ensures that Qcells USA projects deliver exceptional value and performance. With several multi-billion-dollar investments, Qcells is pioneering the establishment of the only complete module supply chain in the U.S., including the expansion of our Georgia module manufacturing facility, which stands as the largest in the Western Hemisphere.
 
 
As an integral part of the global Qcells brand, Qcells USA benefits from a legacy of excellence in photovoltaic manufacturing. Qcells is renowned worldwide for its high-performance, superior-quality solar cells and modules. With dual headquarters in Seoul, South Korea (Global Executive HQ) and Thalheim, Germany (Technology & Innovation HQ), Qcells operates under the umbrella of Hanwha Group, a FORTUNE Global 500 company and one of the top 8 business conglomerates in South Korea.
 
 
**Summary**
The SVP, Environment, Safety, Health & Quality (ESHQ) provides senior executive leadership over all environmental, safety, health, and quality programs across Qcells USA's EPC construction operations. This role is accountable for developing and executing the company's integrated ESHQ strategy, driving a zero-incident safety culture, embedding construction quality excellence into every phase of project delivery, ensuring regulatory compliance, and managing ESHQ performance across active utility-scale solar PV and BESS project sites nationwide.
 
 
Working in close partnership with EPC project leadership, site teams, subcontractors, and corporate stakeholders, the SVP, ESHQ sets the enterprise standard for environmental stewardship, occupational health, construction safety, and quality management. This role serves as the primary ESHQ authority for the EPC business, owns the company's Quality Management System (QMS), and represents Qcells USA with regulatory agencies, clients, certification bodies, and industry organizations. This position reports to the COO, or another management personnel that the CEO of the Company may designate. This position is hybrid, based out of our Houston, TX office, requiring up to 4 days per week in the office. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8:00am to 5:00pm or 9:00am to 6:00pm local time. This position is expected to travel up to 40%.
 
 
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

source.title: Deputy Head of Production, Connected Warfare
source.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE SITE 

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1 , its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.



 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Connected Warfare will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1 , our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. This team will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for 3 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

 ABOUT THE ROLE 

 As the Connected Warfare Deputy Head of Production, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of defense manufacturing by directly influencing the production of Anduril’s Connected Warfare product line. Working as a right hand to the Head of Production, you will own the short-to-mid-term strategic development and execution of manufacturing operations, driving products from NPI to full-rate production. This role requires a dynamic leader who can serve as both a strategic architect and a hands-on executor, leading cross-functional teams to meet aggressive timelines and deliver products of the highest quality for our customers. You will contribute significantly to Anduril’s vision of becoming a next-generation aerospace and defense manufacturer.

 

 What You'll Do: 

 
 Production Ownership & Strategy: Own all production outcomes for the Connected Warfare product line, including ramp plans, headcount, and the standing up of new manufacturing lines. Develop and execute a strategy to rapidly scale production volumes f rom NPI to full-rate production.

 Leadership & Team Management: Serve as a strategic leader and tactical do-er, driving all people and resources across production to achieve outcomes. Lead cross-functional teams (including Production, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering) through strong leadership, advocacy, and a consistent on-site presence, holding them accountable to meeting demands, deadlines, and goals.

 Operational Excellence: Drive processes and systems needed throughout the product development lifecycle to mature products to full-rate production. Establish and manage the team to key performance indicators (KPIs) for financial, quality, and on-time delivery, and partner on production budgets and cost targets to optimize manufacturing operations’ impact on the business.

 Quality & Compliance: Be accountable to AS9100D guidelines and drive a “quality-first” culture across all manufacturing operations.

 Process & Technology Advancement: Advise on development and oversee the implementation of digital technologies, from PLM and ERP to our custom MES and QMS systems, that enable our production operations to efficiently scale while meeting customer requirements. Shape corporate tools and processes to support the unique needs of aerospace production.

 
 Required Qualifications: 

 
 8+ years of proven experience overseeing the production and test of complex electromechanical products.

 Strong leadership experience managing large (100+ person) manufacturing teams and directing large cross-functional teams across planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, quality, and production to deliver products of the highest quality.

 A strong background in quality assurance, with a track record of driving a "quality-first" culture in a production environment and accountability to standards like AS9100D.

 Past success operating in both low-rate prototype and high-rate manufacturing environments, with a proven ability to scale production.

 High ownership and the ability to effectively manage multiple large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.

 Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

 Ability to work onsite five days a week at our Asheville, OH campus (Arsenal 1).

 
 Preferred Qualifications: 

 
 Success scaling production operations in a high-complexity manufacturing environment.

 Deep experience with the niche supply chains for aerospace and robotics.

 Demonstrated experience implementing and leveraging digital manufacturing technologies (PLM, ERP, MES, QMS) to drive efficiency and scale.

 
  
 US Salary Range
 $190,000 — $252,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


  

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .   

  

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

source.title: Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing (Contract Manufacturing)
source.description:
**Who we are**

With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility.

**What we need**

Symbotic is seeking a Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing to join our Strategic Sourcing team within our Supply Chain organization. Your role will be to lead our contract manufacturing strategy and develop a resilient, cost-competitive global manufacturing network for complex electromechanical products.

**What we do**

Our global procurement organization partners closely with the business to build category strategies that drive competitive advantage. We own strategic sourcing and supplier agreements end-to-end — from commercial and pricing structures through supplier relationship management — while our sourcing operations ensure disciplined execution at scale. Our scope spans the full lifecycle: procuring robotics, structural, and automation components at the core of our systems, sourcing third-party partners for installation and deployment, and ensuring robust aftersales support once systems are live — all in service of Symbotic's commitment to reimagining the supply chain and transforming the movement of goods through intelligent automation, while bringing unparalleled value to the customer. Every decision is grounded in a relentless focus on total cost of ownership, balancing speed and rigor to drive the best outcomes for the business.

**What you'll do**

* Lead Symbotic's contract manufacturing strategy, including selection, negotiation, onboarding, and ongoing management of global manufacturing partners.
* Own commercial relationships with key contract manufacturers and assembly suppliers, driving cost, quality, delivery, and capacity performance.
* Develop and execute sourcing strategies for complex electromechanical products, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing teams.
* Negotiate long-term supply agreements, manufacturing service agreements (MSAs), pricing, tooling, inventory, and capacity commitments.
* Drive annual cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, should-cost analysis, productivity programs, and supply base optimization.
* Support new product introduction (NPI) and production ramp activities to ensure suppliers meet schedule, quality, and cost objectives.
* Lead executive-level supplier business reviews and establish performance management scorecards and corrective action processes.
* Assess and mitigate supply chain risks related to capacity, geographic concentration, financial stability, and component availability.
* Partner with commodity sourcing teams across mechanical, electronics, motors, batteries, and other key categories to optimize total system cost.
* Develop manufacturing footprint strategies to support business growth, scalability, resiliency, and customer requirements.
* Manage significant annual spend and contribute to long-range supply chain, inventory, and working capital strategies.
* Build and mentor a high-performing sourcing organization as the business scales.

**What you'll need**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree or MBA is highly preferred.
* Minimum 8–10 years of strategic sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, or procurement experience in robotics, automation, industrial equipment, electronics, or other complex hardware industries.
* Minimum 3 years of people management experience leading and growing teams.
* Deep experience managing contract manufacturers or similar EMS/mechanical assembly providers.
* Proven track record negotiating complex commercial agreements and delivering measurable cost reductions.

source.description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.” As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way. We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.

 

The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities: *we come together*, *we always look for a better way*, and *we create possibilities*.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

Interested in joining us on our journey?

 
The Senior Director - Plant Manager executes the business strategy focused on safety, quality, delivery, cost, and morale of the Camden, South Carolina water heater plant. The Plant Manager will work to continuously improve the organization as well as standardize where possible with other facilities in the appliance business. Additionally, this role collaborates closely with Product Management, Technology, Sourcing, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and Central Quality to develop and execute NPI (new product introduction) strategies.

**Position**
------------

Senior Director, Plant Management

**Location**
------------

USA, Camden, SC

**How You'll Create Possibilities**
-----------------------------------

The Senior Director - Plant Manager executes the business strategy focused on safety, quality, delivery, cost, and morale of the Camden, South Carolina water heater plant. The Plant Manager will work to continuously improve the organization as well as standardize where possible with other facilities in the appliance business. Additionally, this role collaborates closely with Product Management, Technology, Sourcing, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and Central Quality to develop and execute NPI (new product introduction) strategies.

**What You'll Bring to Our Team**
---------------------------------

**Minimum Requirements:**

* BS in either Engineering, Operations Management or Supply Chain
* 15+ years of leadership experience in a Manufacturing environment
* Background and demonstrated technical depth in assembly operations and metal fabrication
* Demonstrated ability to drive change and cultural transformation
* Excellent analytical and complex problem-solving skills
* Demonstrated operational leadership abilities and strong communication/change management skills
* Strong business and financial acumen to include critical daily KPI management
* Demonstrated organizational savvy to work cross-functionally to deliver the desired business results
* Appliance, automotive or consumer goods experience gained in a high volume, short cycle, manufacturing environment
* Strong Lean experience with a history of driving a continuous improvement culture
* Demonstrated ability to work and lead collaboratively in a dynamic environment with both salaried and hourly personnel to deliver business financial objectives, NPI program launches and ultimately meet the needs of our customers

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* MS or MBA preferred

**Our Culture**
---------------

Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 
 
This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 
 
By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy.

GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization.

GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S

*If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance or an accommodation to use our website or to apply, please send an e-mail* *to ask.recruiting@geappliances.com*

source.description:
TOGETHER, WE SAVE LIVES
 
 
Summary
 
The Operations Director is responsible for developing and executing the operations strategy for the Jacksonville body armor manufacturing facility. This role provides site leadership across manufacturing operations, manufacturing engineering, maintenance, continuous improvement, and operational excellence to ensure safe, efficient, and scalable execution aligned with company objectives.
 
The Operations Director serves as a champion of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and the Cadre Operating Model, driving a culture of continuous improvement while building organizational structures, leadership capability, and operational systems that support growth and deliver exceptional customer outcomes.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Develop and execute the operations strategy to support facility performance, growth, profitability, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence.
* Lead manufacturing operations and manufacturing engineering functions to achieve safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and productivity objectives.
* Partner cross functionally with Sales, Supply Chain, Engineering, Product Development, Customer Service, Quality, and HR to align operational capabilities with business priorities.
* Establish performance goals, KPIs, and accountability systems that drive results across the organization.
* Lead capacity planning, labor planning, capital investment, and operational readiness for growth, new products, and facility expansion.
* Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and structured problem solving methodologies to improve operational performance.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on throughput, quality, lead time reduction, waste elimination, labor efficiency, and cost optimization.
* Provide strategic oversight of automation, process improvement, manufacturing technology, and capital projects to enhance operational capability and scalability.
* Ensure compliance with safety, quality, regulatory, customer, and environmental requirements while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.
* Build organizational capability through leadership development, succession planning, workforce planning, and organizational design.
* Manage operational budgets and business performance through data-driven decision making, operational reviews, and corrective action planning.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

Education
 

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business, or related field required.
* Master's degree preferred.

Experience
 

* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 5+ years leading managers and multi-functional operational organizations.
* Proven experience leading manufacturing operations in a complex, high-mix manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated success implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and Operational Excellence systems.
* Strong experience leading organizational transformation, culture change, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing manufacturing engineering, automation, capital projects, and process improvement programs.
* Background in ballistic armor, protective equipment, defense, aerospace, composites, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments preferred.
* Experience working within environments requiring strict quality, traceability, regulatory, and customer compliance standards.

Preferred Certifications
 

* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt.

Key Competencies

source.title: Director of Operations
source.description:
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day operations at Innova's M3 facility in Mexicali, Mexico, including production, maintenance, purchasing, shipping and receiving, and site safety. Working closely with the site leadership team, this role ensures production goals, quality standards, cost targets, and customer delivery commitments are met. The Director builds and develops a strong local team, drives continuous improvement, and serves as the key link between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Finance, Quality, and Sales teams. The ideal candidate is based in the San Diego area, is fully bilingual in English and Spanish, and has proven experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico.

 

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Champion and uphold the company's values, mission, and quality policy in all activities.

* Adhere to and help enforce company policies, procedures, and internal control standards.

* Ensure compliance with all applicable Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Follow all safety rules and PPE requirements, and promptly report hazards, incidents, and near-misses.

* Lead all operations at the M3 facility, including production, maintenance, purchasing, and shipping and receiving, to meet production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery commitments.

* Direct and develop the site leadership team, including hiring, training, performance management, and succession planning.

* Oversee production planning and scheduling to balance capacity, labor, and materials with customer demand.

* Establish operational KPIs and monitor productivity, efficiency, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery, taking corrective action as needed.

* Oversee the site safety program and ensure compliance with applicable Mexican health, safety, and environmental regulations (e.g., STPS and NOM standards), fostering a strong culture of safety.

* Develop and manage the site operating budget, labor plan, and capital expenditure requests.

* Oversee equipment maintenance and facility upkeep to maximize uptime and maintain a safe, organized plant.

* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, improve throughput, and lower costs.

* Coordinate with logistics and customs partners to support cross-border shipments, materials flow, and import/export requirements.

* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, employee relations, and compliance with Mexican labor law.

* Serve as the primary liaison between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Quality, Finance, and Sales, providing regular operational and financial reporting.

* Perform other related duties as required.

 

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, required.

* Experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico (maquiladora or similar cross-border environment) strongly preferred.

* Experience with plastics manufacturing processes (e.g., injection molding, thermoforming, CNC machining) preferred.

* Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma certification preferred.

 

**SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (written and verbal) required.

* Proven leadership skills, with the ability to build, motivate, and develop a high-performing team.

* Extensive knowledge of manufacturing operations, production planning, and plant management.

* Strong working knowledge of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.

* Financial acumen, with the ability to develop budgets, manage costs, and interpret financial data.

* Working knowledge of Mexican labor, safety, and environmental regulations.

* Working knowledge of quality system requirements under ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ERP/MRP systems.

* Valid passport and ability to cross the U.S.–Mexico border regularly.

 

**TRAINING & COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS**

* Complete new-hire orientation and role-specific on-the-job training prior to performing unsupervised work.

* Complete Quality Management System (QMS) training applicable to this role, including quality policy awareness and the consequences of nonconformance to product or process requirements.

* Complete safety training applicable to this role (e.g., PPE use, lockout/tagout, forklift certification).

* Maintain competency through periodic refresher or retraining as required by department procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

 

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Office setting.

* Manufacturing floor environment.

* Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses.

 

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

* Mobility to navigate the production floor to conduct inspections and oversight.

 

**EXPECTED HOURS OF WORK**

* This is a full-time exempt position, required to work Monday through Friday. Occasional weekend availability may be required based on business needs.

 

**TRAVEL**

* Regular cross-border travel between San Diego, CA and the M3 facility in Mexicali, with on-site presence required a minimum of 4 days per week.

* Occasional travel to other Innova facilities, customers, and suppliers, up to 10%.

source.title: Senior Manager, Site Reliability Engineering & Operations
source.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
 
 
**Position Summary**
The
**Senior Manager, Site Reliability Engineering & Operations**
is a highly visible leadership role within the Member & Client Services Engineering (MCSE) organization at CVS Health. This position is responsible for ensuring the reliability, availability, performance, and operational excellence of business-critical platforms that support millions of members, customer service operations, clinical services, and enterprise applications. In this role, you will lead the strategy and execution of Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), production operations, observability, incident management, and operational automation across a complex technology ecosystem. You will partner closely with engineering, infrastructure, architecture, and managed service providers to deliver highly reliable, scalable, and resilient technology solutions that support CVS Health's mission.
 
 
The ideal candidate is a strong technical leader with experience driving reliability engineering practices, operational excellence, and continuous improvement in large-scale enterprise environments. You will play a key role in advancing modern SRE capabilities, including AI-driven operations (AIOps), observability, automation, and proactive service reliability initiatives. As a people leader, you will build and develop high-performing teams, influence strategic technology decisions, and foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous learning. This role requires a passion for solving complex operational challenges, improving customer experiences, and driving measurable business outcomes through technology excellence.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Leadership
* Execute and advance the enterprise SRE strategy, including Service Level Objectives (SLOs), Service Level Indicators (SLIs), error budgets, and reliability roadmaps.
* Establish reliability standards and best practices across applications, APIs, data platforms, and emerging AI-powered solutions.
* Champion a culture of reliability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across engineering teams.
* Drive platform resiliency, scalability, performance, and risk mitigation initiatives.

**AI-Driven Operations (AIOps) & Automation**

* Lead the adoption of AIOps capabilities to improve proactive issue detection, predictive analytics, and operational efficiency.
* Implement AI-assisted incident management, automated remediation, self-healing capabilities, and standardized operational runbooks.
* Partner with AI and platform engineering teams to integrate machine learning and generative AI technologies into operational workflows.

**Observability & Monitoring**

* Define and lead the enterprise observability strategy across metrics, logs, traces, and user experience monitoring.
* Drive standardization and adoption of observability platforms such as Datadog, Dynatrace, Splunk, Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry.
* Deliver actionable insights, dashboards, and executive reporting related to platform health, availability, performance, and reliability metrics.

**Incident Management & Operational Excellence**

* Lead enterprise incident response, escalation management, and post-incident reviews.
* Reduce Mean Time to Detect (MTTD), Mean Time to Restore (MTTR), and recurring incidents through automation and preventive engineering practices.
* Establish operational readiness standards, on-call processes, and service management best practices.
* Drive root-cause analysis, problem management, and long-term service stability initiatives.

**Leadership & Talent Development**

* Build, mentor, and lead high-performing global SRE and operations teams.
* Develop career growth frameworks, skill development programs, and technical leadership capabilities.
* Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous learning.
* Partner with stakeholders across technology and business organizations to align reliability priorities with business objectives.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent work experience required, one additional year of experience is required for each year of college not attained.
* 10+ or more years of production support or service delivery experience.
* Experience working with a managed services vendor.
* ITIL Qualified & Expert knowledge of ITIL disciplines.
* Experience of managing 3rd parties and 3rd party delivered services.
* Service Management or Support in a large-scale and diverse environment of incident management, escalation procedures and related disciplines.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* High degree of self-motivation to work in a fast-paced dynamic environment.
* Strong communication skills are required to facilitate meetings with both technical and business audiences, often across multiple functional departments.
* Demonstrated understanding of various technologies (Java/J2EE, .Net, MQ, Mainframe, Telephony systems etc.)
* Experience with major database management systems, e.g. DB2, Oracle, and SQL Server.
* Experience creatively debugging complex system problems spanning entire hosting stack (application, server, communication channels, networking components, etc), resulting in problem determination and restoration through thorough research and fact finding.
* Be able to exhibit decisiveness and good judgment, even in ambiguous circumstances.
* Experience supporting both proprietary and vendor developed or supported applications.
* Demonstrated successful completion of technical projects.
* Demonstrated proficiency working on all phases of SDLC.
* Able to exhibit decisiveness and good judgment, even in ambiguous circumstances.

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent work experience required, one additional year of experience is required for each year of college not attained.
* ITIL certified

**Pay Range**
**The Typical Pay Range For This Role Is**
$106,605.00 - $213,210.00
 
 
This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.
 
 
Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.
 
 
**Great Benefits For Great People**
We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.
 
 
This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.
 
 
Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.
 
 
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 11/30/2026
 
 
Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

Who we are 
 With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. 
 
 What we need 
 Symbotic is seeking a Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing to join our Strategic Sourcing team within our Supply Chain organization. Your role will be to lead our contract manufacturing strategy and develop a resilient, cost-competitive global manufacturing network for complex electromechanical products.

 What we do 
 Our global procurement organization partners closely with the business to build category strategies that drive competitive advantage. We own strategic sourcing and supplier agreements end-to-end — from commercial and pricing structures through supplier relationship management — while our sourcing operations ensure disciplined execution at scale. Our scope spans the full lifecycle: procuring robotics, structural, and automation components at the core of our systems, sourcing third-party partners for installation and deployment, and ensuring robust aftersales support once systems are live — all in service of Symbotic's commitment to reimagining the supply chain and transforming the movement of goods through intelligent automation, while bringing unparalleled value to the customer. Every decision is grounded in a relentless focus on total cost of ownership, balancing speed and rigor to drive the best outcomes for the business.

 What you'll do 
 Lead Symbotic's contract manufacturing strategy, including selection, negotiation, onboarding, and ongoing management of global manufacturing partners.
 Own commercial relationships with key contract manufacturers and assembly suppliers, driving cost, quality, delivery, and capacity performance.
 Develop and execute sourcing strategies for complex electromechanical products, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing teams.
 Negotiate long-term supply agreements, manufacturing service agreements (MSAs), pricing, tooling, inventory, and capacity commitments.
 Drive annual cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, should-cost analysis, productivity programs, and supply base optimization.
 Support new product introduction (NPI) and production ramp activities to ensure suppliers meet schedule, quality, and cost objectives.
 Lead executive-level supplier business reviews and establish performance management scorecards and corrective action processes.
 Assess and mitigate supply chain risks related to capacity, geographic concentration, financial stability, and component availability.
 Partner with commodity sourcing teams across mechanical, electronics, motors, batteries, and other key categories to optimize total system cost.
 Develop manufacturing footprint strategies to support business growth, scalability, resiliency, and customer requirements.
 Manage significant annual spend and contribute to long-range supply chain, inventory, and working capital strategies.
 Build and mentor a high-performing sourcing organization as the business scales. 
 
 What you'll need 
 Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management , Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree or MBA is highly preferred.   
 Minimum 8–10 years of strategic sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, or procurement experience in robotics, automation, industrial equipment, electronics, or other complex hardware industries.
 Minimum 3 years of people management experience leading and growing teams.
 Deep experience managing contract manufacturers or similar EMS/mechanical assembly providers.
 Proven track record negotiating complex commercial agreements and delivering measurable cost reductions.
 Experience supporting product launches, manufacturing transfers, and global production ramp-ups.
 Strong understanding of electromechanical systems, including mechanical assemblies, motors, electronics, batteries, and custom manufactured components.
 Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and effectively communicate with executive leadership and strategic suppliers.
 Demonstrated leadership experience managing teams and driving results in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. 
 
 Our Environment 
 Up to 20% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ.
 Employees may be required to use a personal credit card for business travel expenses, which are reimbursed based on the program guidelines. Eligible employees may receive a corporate credit card based on role and travel requirements, but a personal credit card may be needed during onboarding until the corporate card is issued.
